name: Binary Search on Answer
description: When the problem asks to minimize/maximize some value and you can write a monotonic 'is this value feasible?' check, binary search over the answer space instead of the input array.
core_technique: Define a feasibility function f(x) that's monotonic (true for all x >= some threshold, false below it). Binary search over the range of possible answers, calling f(mid) to decide which half to keep.
common_pitfalls: Forgetting to prove/verify monotonicity before applying binary search -- if the feasibility function isn't monotonic, this pattern silently gives wrong answers; incorrect boundary handling (lo=mid vs lo=mid+1 depending on which half is kept).

example_problems.title: Koko Eating Bananas
example_problems.why_it_fits: Binary search over possible eating speeds; feasibility check is 'can Koko finish all bananas at this speed within h hours' -- monotonic in speed.

example_problems.title: Capacity To Ship Packages Within D Days
example_problems.why_it_fits: Same shape -- binary search over ship capacity, feasibility check simulates whether that capacity ships everything in D days.

example_problems.title: Split Array Largest Sum
example_problems.why_it_fits: Binary search over the 'largest subarray sum' answer, feasibility check greedily partitions and counts subarrays needed.

additional_considerations: This pattern is easy to miss because the problem doesn't mention 'sorted' or 'search' at all -- the signal is 'minimize the maximum' or 'find the smallest x such that a condition holds.' Always state the feasibility function and argue monotonicity out loud in an interview before coding.
